How long the app can stay in the background before it locks. Locking also forgets the search, the open screens and everything loaded.

On: downloads go on after the lock. Until they finish, the files\' addresses, the tags, the sources with their credentials and the sites\' cookies stay in RAM. Files on storage stay encrypted; once the queue is done, everything is dropped from memory.
Off: on lock the queue is encrypted in the vault and paused, and it resumes at the next unlock. No download data stays in RAM.
Blocks screenshots and screen recordings and hides the preview in recent apps. Always on while the app is locked.
Google Safe Browsing in the built-in browser
Unavailable: in the WebView, Safe Browsing works through Google Play services, which this phone does not have. No address is sent to Google either way.

On. For every address the built-in browser opens (pages, images, scripts, ads included) Google Play services computes a cryptographic fingerprint and compares it with a list kept on the phone. When the start of the fingerprint matches an entry in the list, it sends that fragment of a few bytes to Google\'s servers for confirmation. Google does not receive the address in clear, but sees your IP, the time and the fragment; the request comes from the phone\'s Google services, so it can be linked to the device, and it does NOT go through Tor even when Tor is on. In return, a page known for malware, phishing or unwanted software is blocked with a warning.

Off: the built-in browser does not consult Google and no data about the addresses you visit is sent to it. You get no warning if a page is known for malware or phishing. This only concerns the built-in browser: the app\'s searches, images and downloads never use Safe Browsing.
Passed anti-bot checks and sessions, encrypted in the vault
Irreversibly erases content, settings, sources and the key.

Content, settings, sources, cookies and the download queue are encrypted in the vault with AES-256-GCM, with keys derived through ECDH P-256. The private key is protected by Argon2id (64 MiB) and, if enabled, by a biometric Keystore key. Browsed images stay in memory only.

All of the app\'s connections go through the Tor network via Orbot: searches, images, videos, downloads and the built-in browser. Sites see the address of a Tor node instead of yours, and site names are resolved inside Tor too (no DNS request in clear). If Orbot is not running nothing loads: the app never falls back to a direct connection. It is slower, and some sites block Tor or ask for the anti-bot check more often. Tor hides where you connect from, not who you are: a site you are logged in to, or that recognises its own cookies, still knows your account, while everything else just sees another Tor user. For browsing that should stay apart from an account, stay logged out, or clear the site\'s cookies in the Data section.
Default 9050. The app connects only to this port on this phone. It does not take the port from Orbot\'s status messages, which any app could send.

For maximum coverage also turn on Orbot\'s VPN mode with BooruVault selected: it catches every packet at system level, even outside the proxy.

Orbot is the Tor Project\'s official app for Android and bridges to the Tor network. Install it, open it once, then turn this option back on.\n\n“Search the stores” lets you choose among the installed stores (F-Droid, Droid-ify, Aurora, Play…). If your F-Droid store does not find it, add the Guardian Project repository or download the APK from Orbot\'s website.

Reads the site through its API: posts arrive complete (file, size, md5, tags by type), pages are small and quick, and what the vault already holds is recognised. Some content may need an account or a key.

Reads the site\'s web pages, as a browser would: no API or key is needed, and sites without an API work too. In return each post is opened on its own to find its file, loading is slower and heavier, less is known about a post (no size or md5 to recognise duplicates), anti-bot checks come more often, and a redesign of the site can break it.

With a user ID and key the site is read through its API; without them, through its web pages, with the costs of that: each post opened on its own, slower loading, less known about a post, more anti-bot checks.

These options weaken the protections BooruVault gives you by default. Read what each one does before turning it on.
Read protected pages with a hidden browser

On: when a site keeps asking for the anti-bot check even after you passed it (common with Tor), the app opens its pages in a hidden browser and reads them from there. For every page read this way the site\'s JavaScript runs as in a normal visit, trackers included, and can take a fingerprint of the browser. Third-party cookies stay blocked, WebRTC stays off, images are not loaded, traffic goes through Tor when Tor is on, and the browser\'s data is erased after each page. It is slower and uses more battery.
Off: when a site keeps asking for the anti-bot check, the app stops and asks you to pass it in the built-in browser. The site\'s code runs only while you are looking at it.
Open links outside Tor when Tor Browser is missing

On: with Tor on and no Tor Browser, a link can still be opened in a normal browser after a warning that holds the button for a few seconds. That browser does not use Tor: the site sees your real IP address, and the visit may stay in its history, cookies and cache, or be synced to an account.
Off: with Tor on, links open in Tor Browser. Without it, a link can only be copied, to paste in a browser that goes through Orbot.
Exact tags, as on the boorus: -tag excludes, ~tag for alternatives, * as a wildcard. Also type:video, type:gif, type:image, source:name and rating:general|sensitive|questionable|explicit.

The site would see your real IP address, and the browser may keep the visit in its history, cookies and cache, or sync it to an account.\n\nTo stay on Tor, install Tor Browser, or copy the link and open it in a browser that goes through Orbot.

Install it, or copy the link and paste it in a browser that goes through Orbot.\n\nTo be able to open links in a normal browser anyway, exposing your real IP address, turn on “Open links outside Tor” in the risky options.
